backlog.spec: Change the very first start (and any start=None call) so it does not use uniform random centres. Pick a row pattern at random from [[5,5,6,5,5],[6,5,6,5,4]... restricted to patterns summing to 26, e.g. [5,5,6,5,5],[5,6,5,5,5],[6,5,5,5,5],[4,5,4,5,4,4]]. Place the rows at equally spaced y values in (0,1). Within each row, space the circles evenly in x with an alternating half-spacing offset. Add Gaussian jitter with sd 0.02 drawn from rng, clip to [0.05, 0.95], and set the initial radii to 0.05. Then run phase 1 and phase 2 as before. Near-hexagonal starts land closer to the known optimum's basin than uniform noise does.
backlog.title: Structured row-based initial layouts

backlog.spec: Choose the kick disc centre p near a circle selected with probability proportional to 1/r_i, where r_i is its radius in the incumbent, so that small (loosely held) circles are more likely to be perturbed. Set p to that circle's centre plus a small uniform offset of at most 0.05, then apply the existing disc re-randomisation with R drawn as before. This focuses the kick on circles that have the most room to move, instead of on a uniformly random point of the square.
backlog.title: Small-circle-biased kick selection

backlog.spec: In solve, lower the main loop limit to 0.75*time_limit. After the loop, take the best (c, r) and run phase 2 of _solve_once once more from np.concatenate([c.ravel(), r]), using SLSQP options maxiter=1000 and ftol=1e-13. Clip the centres to [0,1] and run _repair. Keep the polished result only if its radius sum is larger than best's. Return best. The goal is to recover the slack that SLSQP's default ftol of 1e-6 leaves in the result. Add a parameter `ftol` to _solve_once (default None, meaning SLSQP's default) so this is a small change.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish of best

backlog.spec: After the main loop in solve, take best (c, r) and run _solve_once(n, rng, start=np.concatenate([c.ravel(), r])) one more time, but with SLSQP options {'maxiter': 1000, 'ftol': 1e-14} for this call only: add an optional argument polish=False to _solve_once that switches the phase-2 options. Then clip, _repair, and replace best only if the repaired sum is larger. The 20% time slack left by TIME_FRACTION covers this one solve. This closes the gap between the loose 200-iteration optimum and the true local optimum.
backlog.title: Final high-precision SLSQP polish of best

backlog.spec: Replace the disc re-randomisation with a band kick. With probability 0.5 choose a horizontal band, otherwise a vertical band, at a random offset. The band width is uniform in [0.1, 0.3] and it spans the full square. Select the circles whose centres fall inside the band, re-randomise their centres uniformly inside the band, set their radii to 0, and re-optimise with _solve_once as before. This changes the shape of the perturbed region while keeping the rest of the kick loop identical.
backlog.title: Strip kick instead of disc kick

backlog.spec: Count consecutive kicks without improvement. If the count reaches 60, start a new chain: run a fresh random _solve_once(n, rng) (phase 1 + phase 2), clip and repair it, and make it the chain's current state, so later kicks perturb this new state. Keep a separate global best over all chains and return it. Reset the counter on any chain improvement or restart. Only run a restart while at least 25% of the time budget remains, so new chains have time to mature.
backlog.title: Stagnation restart of the kick chain

backlog.spec: Replace the disc kick with a count-based kick. Draw a random point p in [0,1]^2 and let k be a random integer in [3, 10]. Re-randomise the centres of the k circles nearest to p, placing each new centre uniformly in a disc of radius 0.2 around p and clipping to the square. Set their radii to 0 and re-optimise with _solve_once as before. Each kick then touches a fixed number of circles regardless of local density.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour kick

backlog.spec: With probability 0.2, a kick takes the best packing and reflects the centres and radii of all circles with x > 0.5 across the line x = 0.5 (or y = 0.5, chosen at random). It then sets the radii of circles within 0.1 of the mirror line to 0 and re-optimises. This gives mirrored copies of good halves as starts. Accept by the existing rule.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric kick halves

backlog.spec: In the local-kick branch, keep the disc selection m (p uniform, R in [0.15, 0.35]) but do not re-randomise the selected centres uniformly. Instead add Gaussian noise c[m] += rng.normal(0, 0.5*R, (k, 2)), clip to [0, 1], and set r[m] *= 0.3 instead of 0. The kicked state stays closer to the incumbent's structure while still breaking local contacts. Everything else stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Partial-radius jitter kick instead of full re-randomisation

backlog.spec: Change the first-start initialisation in _solve_once. Instead of giving every circle radius INIT_RADIUS and uniform centres, draw initial radii from a uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.12] per circle and draw centres uniformly in [0.05, 0.95]. Use these for the first phase too. Also use a fresh random restart with probability 0.2 on each iteration, so that a fraction of the budget explores new regions rather than only local kicks. Both choices add diversity across seeds.
backlog.title: Non-uniform radius initialisation and random restarts mix

backlog.spec: Track the success rate of recent kicks over a sliding window of the last 20 attempts, counting a success when the new sum beats the best. Scale the kick radius range (currently 0.15 to 0.35 for the disc kick) up when the success rate is below 0.1 and down when it is above 0.3, clamped to [0.05, 0.5]. Also scale the Gaussian noise sd in the basin-hopping move the same way. This removes the hand-tuned kick size and adapts it to the difficulty of the instance during the run.
backlog.title: Adaptive kick strength from acceptance history

backlog.spec: In solve, replace the fixed kick radius R ~ U(0.15, 0.35) with an adaptive R. Keep a scalar R_mean, starting at 0.25, and draw R = clip(R_mean * exp(rng.normal(0, 0.3)), 0.08, 0.4). After each kick, if it improved best, set R_mean = 0.8*R_mean + 0.2*R. Otherwise grow R_mean by 1% toward 0.25 every 10 failed kicks. Also, instead of always setting the kicked radii to 0, set them to 0.5 * their old value. This keeps more structure and gives finer late-stage refinement.
backlog.title: Smaller, adaptive kick radius

backlog.spec: In solve, alternate between the existing disc kick and a new kick, choosing each with probability 0.5. The new kick: pick k = rng.integers(1, 4) circles, chosen from the 6 with the smallest radii. Move each one to the best of 200 random candidate points in [0,1]^2, where best means the point that maximises the clearance min(min_j(|p - c_j| - r_j), the distance to the nearest wall). Leave out the moved circles when computing clearance. Set the moved radii to 0, then call _solve_once with that start vector as the disc kick does. This targets the known weak spot of local optima: small circles stuck in poor holes.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circles kick

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, give SLSQP exact gradients so it does not use finite differences. Pass jac for the objective: for phase 2 the gradient of -sum(r) is zeros on the centres and -1 on the radii; for phase 1 it is -1 on the t entry. Add a 'jac' function to each constraint dict that returns the dense Jacobian (rows = constraints, cols = variables). For each pair row k=(i,j): d(dist)/dc_i = (c_i-c_j)/dist, d/dc_j = -(c_i-c_j)/dist, -1 on r_i and r_j (or -2 on t in phase 1). Guard dist with max(dist,1e-12). The boundary rows are +1 or -1 on the relevant coordinate and -1 on r_i (or t). The nonnegativity row is +1 on r_i. Build the Jacobian with numpy fancy indexing into a preallocated zero matrix. Change nothing else. Within the same time budget this should give many more kicks.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a second kick type, chosen with probability 0.3. Pick two random points p and q. Swap the centres of the circles inside the two small discs of radius 0.15 (match the counts by taking the k nearest circles to each point), set their radii to 0 and re-optimise via _solve_once. Accept it by the same rule as the other kicks.
backlog.title: Swap-and-kick of two discs

backlog.spec: Rewrite the pair constraints in cons and cons_eq in squared form: dx^2 + dy^2 - (ri + rj)^2 >= 0, which avoids the sqrt. Add the analytic Jacobian for them. Keep the wall constraints linear. Check that the repair step still makes the packing valid. The aim is faster and smoother SLSQP, so there are more kicks per run.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints

backlog.spec: Use MAX_ITER=100 for kick re-optimisations to get more attempts, and when a candidate is within 0.002 of the best, polish it with an additional SLSQP run of 500 iterations and ftol=1e-12. This gives accurate convergence only for the promising candidates.
backlog.title: Lower MAX_ITER for kicks, higher for final polish

backlog.spec: In the kick, replace the np.clip of the re-randomised centres with reflection at the walls. For each coordinate x outside [0,1], set x to -x if x < 0 and to 2-x if x > 1, then clip once more to [0,1] for safety. The current clip piles displaced circles onto the boundary, which creates a degenerate start for SLSQP. Reflection keeps the kicked points spread out. Keep the rest of the kick loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Reflect rather than clip after kick

backlog.spec: Supply analytic gradients via the jac argument for the objective (constant -1 on radii) and for the constraints (sparse-structure dense matrix built with numpy for pair, wall and positivity constraints), in both phase 1 and phase 2. This removes finite-difference cost (about 80 variables), giving many more restarts and kicks in the 30 s budget. Keep the constraint ordering identical.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the body of _repair with a linear program. With the centres fixed, maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs i<j, r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i), and r_i >= 0. Use scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs') with c=-ones, A_ub built from the pair indices (np.triu_indices), and b_ub = the pair distances, with bounds (0, wall_dist_i). Return np.maximum(r - SHRINK, 0) as before. If linprog fails, fall back to the existing pairwise-shrink code, kept as a helper. This gives the best valid radii for the given centres instead of the lossy pairwise scaling, so each candidate is scored more fairly.
backlog.title: Optimal radii via LP in repair

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time budget. Stop the kick loop at 0.72*time_limit. Then run SLSQP on the best packing's full (centres, radii) vector, with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-14, restarting from its own output until the sum of radii improves by less than 1e-10. Pass the result through _repair, and keep it only if its sum is larger than the best sum.
backlog.title: Final polish with tight SLSQP

backlog.spec: For the first 25% of the time, run independent random restarts with initial radii drawn from uniform(0.03, 0.12) and keep the top 3 solutions. In the remaining time, apply kicks to randomly chosen members of the top 3 and replace the worst member when improved. This gives a diversity of basins and avoids a single early basin.
backlog.title: Randomised initial radii and population of starts

backlog.spec: Keep a current state cur separate from best. After each kick and repair, accept the new packing as cur if r.sum() > cur_sum - T, where T = 2e-3 * (1 - elapsed/(TIME_FRACTION*time_limit)), so T falls linearly to 0. Update best whenever r.sum() > best_sum. Kicks always start from cur, not best. The first random restart initialises both cur and best. Return best. This is deterministic threshold accepting, not Metropolis, and it lets the chain cross small barriers between nearby basins.
backlog.title: Threshold acceptance on the kick chain

backlog.spec: In solve, track the number of consecutive kicks that have not improved the local incumbent of the current run. When it reaches 30, start a fresh run from a new random start (_solve_once(n, rng) with start=None) and run kicks from that new local incumbent. Keep a global best across all runs and return it. This turns the single-trajectory search into a multi-start search, which lowers the variance across seeds when one seed's first basin is poor.
backlog.title: Periodic fresh restarts with stagnation counter

backlog.spec: In the kick solves, include only the pair constraints for circle pairs whose centre distance is below r_i + r_j + 0.25 in the starting configuration. Run SLSQP with that reduced set. Afterwards check all pairs. If any is violated, re-solve once with the full set from the result. The smaller constraint count should make each solve much faster.
backlog.title: Neighbour-only constraints in kicked solves

backlog.spec: In the local-kick branch of solve, draw the disc centre p as the centre of a randomly chosen circle, p = c[rng.integers(n)] + rng.normal(0, 0.02, 2), instead of p = rng.uniform(0, 1, 2). This makes sure at least one circle is re-randomised (with a uniform p, the disc can fall in an empty region or a corner and the kick then does nothing) and spreads kicks in proportion to circle density. Keep R, the re-randomisation, the r[m] = 0 reset and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Disc centred on a random existing circle

backlog.spec: Add a second kick type in the main loop, chosen with probability 0.5 against the disc kick. Pick the circle with the smallest radius in the incumbent, move its centre to a uniformly random point in [0.05, 0.95]^2 with radius set to 0, and re-optimise with _solve_once from that start. Small circles are the usual weak point of a packing, so relocating them is a targeted escape from local optima.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert move for the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Replace the disc-based kick in solve with a global perturbation: add Gaussian noise with sd drawn uniformly from [0.005, 0.03] to every centre of the incumbent, clip to [0, 1], keep the radii, and re-run _solve_once from that start. Keep the existing acceptance rule (keep the best by sum of radii). This tests whether many small moves around the current basin beat occasional large relocations.
backlog.title: Small-noise basin hopping instead of disc re-randomisation

backlog.spec: Pass a `jac` to both SLSQP calls in _solve_once so the solver does not finite-difference the constraint vector. Build the Jacobian of cons (and cons_eq) analytically: for each pair (i, j) in iu, the distance gradient w.r.t. c[i] and c[j] is (c[i]-c[j])/d and its negative, and the radius terms contribute -1 entries on r[i] and r[j]. Boundary rows are simple sparse ±1 entries on the coordinates and radii. Fill a dense (num_constraints, 3n) matrix with np.add.at or direct indexing, and give the objective a matching gradient. This should cut per-iteration cost by a large factor, so more kicks fit into the 0.8 * 30 s CPU budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP constraints

backlog.spec: Before every kick, apply one of the 8 symmetries of the unit square chosen at random with the seeded rng to the incumbent centres: optionally swap x and y, then optionally replace x by 1-x and/or y by 1-y. The radii are unchanged and the packing stays valid because the square is symmetric. The kick then perturbs a different region of the same packing on each iteration, which changes which local defects are exposed without changing the objective of the incumbent.
backlog.title: Random square-symmetry transform before each kick

memo: Helped: changes to how each solve searches. Slot 8 (equal-radius SLSQP before the free solve) gave -2.6311/-2.6311. Slot 35 (local disc re-randomisation kick) is the incumbent at -2.6343/-2.6354 (delta -0.0037, 2 runs, mean -2.6349). Local-search walks beat fresh restarts: slot 11 gave -2.6354/-2.6334 and slot 27 gave -2.6341/-2.6324. Replica exchange (-2.6348) and the two-island model (-2.6349) tie the incumbent, so more chain machinery adds nothing. No effect (+0.0000): TIME_FRACTION 0.93, LP repair, warm restarts, successive halving. Hurt: radius-weighted restarts (+0.0165), log-barrier (+0.0045), L-BFGS-B penalty (+0.0034), MAX_ITER 1000 (+0.0019). Start-diversity tweaks are exhausted. Next: tune the kick size, disc radius and acceptance rule of slot 35, and polish the best packing at the end. Replicate any gain, since noise sd is 0.0023. Keep the code simple.
